nodes.label: Denoise NAS — GA architecture search for mobile image denoising
nodes.rationale: Evolves image-denoising architectures for resource-constrained edge/mobile devices by mutating and recombining real DenoiseUnet* seeds, screening with a short training proxy and filtering for on-device deployability, reporting winners on quality (PSNR) vs cost (MACs / TFLite latency) axes.

nodes.label: Two-sibling-repo layout under THESIS_ROOT
nodes.rationale: One virtualenv (nn-dataset's) drives everything; nn-dataset supplies datasets/training/metrics/seeds and nn-gpt supplies the generation engine, so both must be checked out side by side under one root.

nodes.label: TFLite latency caveat (desktop CPU, not phone ms)
nodes.rationale: to_tflite.py measures real XNNPACK inference time on the desktop CPU: it ranks models correctly and correlates with phone cost, but the absolute ms are not phone ms. True on-device numbers need ADB benchmark_model or a hardware-calibrated predictor such as nn-Meter.
nodes.norm_label: tflite latency caveat (desktop cpu, not phone ms)

nodes.label: Fitness eff = PSNR − 0.3·ln(MACs / budget)
nodes.rationale: Combines quality and compute cost into a single scalar so the GA optimises PSNR under a logarithmic compute penalty rather than PSNR alone.

nodes.label: Edge deployability filter (--edge-filter, --mac-cap)
nodes.rationale: Rejects non-TFLite-convertible or over-MAC-cap children before training so GPU time is not spent on undeployable architectures.

nodes.label: Accuracy predictor pre-screen funnel (--predictor)
nodes.rationale: Trains only the top-ranked half of each generation and surrogates the rest, cutting evaluation cost; it only re-ranks within a generation and falls back to measurement.

nodes.label: 5-epoch proxy training screen
nodes.rationale: A short proxy is used to rank candidates cheaply; ep5-on-MAI compresses architecture differences (~1 dB spread) so it must be used to rank, never to report.

nodes.label: Proxy vs. final reporting rule
nodes.rationale: Full training spreads architecture differences ~4x and SIDD ~10x versus the ep5 proxy, so rank on the proxy but report on full-train / SIDD; full-train is the promotion authority.

nodes.label: Per-generation checkpointing and evaluation cache
nodes.rationale: The GA checkpoints after every generation (*_checkpoint.pkl) and caches every evaluated model (*_cache.json) so a restart continues from the last completed generation, never from gen 0; deleting them forces a gen-0 restart.

nodes.label: production_supervisor.sh — crash-resilient wrapper
nodes.rationale: Self-healing supervisor that re-launches the run on crash until it prints '=== DONE', enabling unattended long runs.

nodes.label: sidd_sweep.py — cross-dataset SIDD validation
nodes.rationale: MAI has little headroom so cross-dataset PSNR on SIDD (~+9 dB spread) is what gives the ranking credibility.

nodes.label: promote.py — grow the seed pool from winners
nodes.norm_label: promote.py — grow the seed pool from winners

nodes.label: PSNR metric with PSNR_SCALE = 48
nodes.rationale: The metric stores PSNR x 48; values must be divided by 48 to obtain real dB.

nodes.label: Artifact-level (not bit-exact) reproducibility
nodes.rationale: The GA and training are not bit-seeded, so results reproduce at the architecture/result level only.

nodes.label: Production run resume procedure
nodes.rationale: A detached nohup run survives session expiry but not node teardown; one supervisor command restarts it from the last checkpoint, re-running at most the in-flight generation's un-cached models.

nodes.label: track_autorefresh.sh — predictor tracking monitor
nodes.rationale: Stateless monitor writing predictor_tracking.json + history CSV every 3 generations; safe to lose or restart because it re-scores from the current cache.

nodes.label: Single-production-process rule
nodes.rationale: Never run two production processes against the same namespace; the supervisor guards against this, so launch_production.sh must not be started directly alongside it. Git push/commit stays manual and is never automated.

nodes.rationale: The seed pool is the one input that changes between runs and is not recoverable from the outputs alone, because the GA writes candidates rather than its inputs and the LLM corpus is derived at runtime from whatever the DB held.

nodes.label: mac_audit.py — in-container MAC measurement
nodes.rationale: Treats unmeasurable models as UNKNOWN rather than as a pass, which is the opposite of the fail-open behaviour that let over-cap seeds through.

nodes.label: Fail-open MAC gate hazard
nodes.rationale: _seed_is_edge_legal() returns True on any exception (correct inside the GA so a thop hiccup cannot empty the pool, but indistinguishable from a clean pass); measure_cost() needs torch, absent on the submit node; and its lazy import of mutator.lemur_io lives in a different tree from edge_cost.py, so callers adding only the denoise dir to sys.path get ModuleNotFoundError for every model.

nodes.label: 9053 MMac edge cap
nodes.rationale: Set to exactly DenoiseUnet9F's own measured cost — the largest seed the project happened to own — then cited by seed selection, --edge-filter, the LLM prompt and preflight.py as the edge budget. Circular and never hardware-derived.

nodes.label: DenoiseUnet9F seed (9053 MMac, 35.43 dB)
nodes.rationale: Sits at 99.996% of budget: the highest-PSNR seed with no room to evolve, so its lineage can only shrink and any growing mutation is rejected pre-training. Should be swapped for a seed with headroom if 9F descendants get culled disproportionately.

nodes.label: DenoiseUnet4F — over-cap seed missed by the denylist
nodes.rationale: 12585 MMac (1.4x cap) yet absent from KNOWN_OVER_CAP, which named only 2F/7F/10F per a code comment; the 'just use the F variants' rule admitted it. The live measurement, not the static list, caught it at launch.

nodes.label: ep5 → ep50 Spearman +0.263
nodes.rationale: The measured rank correlation is +0.263, not the 0.90 assumed when the --epoch 5 budget was set, so 5 epochs is a liveness/triage screen and not a quality ranking; headline dB claims need a 50-epoch stage.

nodes.label: --prof-predictor (disabled surrogate)
nodes.rationale: Measured rho=-0.140 / MAE 0.553 dB at n=18, 4.7x worse than predicting the corpus mean; its rho=+0.84 at n=6 did not survive the larger sample, so it was turned off while the built-in --predictor was kept.

nodes.label: DiversityGate — WL graph-hash novelty gate
nodes.rationale: The standard everywhere is EXACT graph-hash novelty; --diversity-graded was never used and --cka-max 0.80 is inert (the CKA-era args are accepted but unused by the WL gate). Exact hashing accepts 'same architecture, rescaled channel widths' at cosine >= 0.985.

nodes.label: Correction: most launchers ran ungated
nodes.rationale: Only R3/R4/R5/WLVAL left *_wlhashes.pt stores, so only those ran gated; A0/B0/C0/D0/BEAT1/P1/P2 were ungated. If the 131 DenoiseGA-* models came from ungated launchers their distinctness was asserted afterwards by offline cosine-0.95 clustering, which is not the same claim as generation-time enforcement.

nodes.label: screen_llm_candidates.py — same diversity bar for LLM output
nodes.rationale: Gates on the exact WL hash and reports cosine as advisory only, so LLM output is judged by the same bar as GA output.
nodes.norm_label: screen_llm_candidates.py — same diversity bar for llm output

nodes.label: Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (32k ctx)
nodes.rationale: Chosen because the 4096-ctx configs in conf/llm/ cannot hold the ~22k-char seeded prompt.

nodes.label: Cold vs seeded prompting arms
nodes.rationale: The arms must differ only in the presence of reference code, or the ablation measures wording instead of conditioning; TASK/CONSTRAINTS/INTERFACE CONTRACT/OUTPUT blocks are byte-identical and verified by --check-contract before generation.

nodes.label: Per-candidate prompt/response archival (prompts.jsonl, run_meta.json)
nodes.rationale: Every prompt, system prompt and raw response is archived per candidate with config sha256s and both repo git revisions, so re-extraction never needs a GPU and runs stay traceable.

nodes.label: out_shape=(1000,) classification-default trap
nodes.rationale: mutator/lemur_io.py injects classification defaults regardless of task, so a denoiser indexing out_shape[1] raises IndexError and scores DEAD for a harness reason rather than an architectural one. Invisible because no hand-written seed indexes out_shape; latent for the GA, and the fix belongs at a run boundary.

nodes.label: Prompt defect: three spatial sizes in one prompt
nodes.rationale: The INTERFACE CONTRACT showed in_shape=(1,3,512,512) copied from DenoiseUnet9F, the TASK block said [B,3,256,256], and the loader passed (1,3,224,224) — models told to size layers from in_shape were set up to fail.
nodes.norm_label: prompt defect: three spatial sizes in one prompt

nodes.label: self.device prompt defect (use without assign)
nodes.rationale: The contract told the model to USE self.device twice and never to ASSIGN it; nn.Module has no .device, so 122/150 cold candidates broke on the first batch versus 3/366 seeded (the seeded arm saw reference code containing the assignment). Screening as-is would have produced a headline about zero-reference prompting that was a pure artefact of the prompt bug, voiding any earlier cold-vs-seeded yield number.

nodes.label: repair_device_attr.py — insert missing self.device line
nodes.rationale: Repair rather than regeneration because the missing line is harness boilerplate that changes no layer, topology or MAC count; discarding 122 architectures over a line the LLM was never asked to write would be the wrong trade. Originals kept as candidate.py.orig and meta.json gains _repaired so repaired models can be excluded from raw-yield claims.

nodes.label: Pod-local LEMUR root (shared scratch dir fix)
nodes.rationale: check_nn writes each candidate into a shared scratch package out/nn/tmp/ and imports it; eight pods against one NFS directory delete each other's module mid-import. It is a race, so a single-GPU smoke test cannot reproduce it. Const.py picks the root by walking up from CWD for a directory holding both ab/ and README.md, so a private root is a directory with those symlinked in. Any future multi-pod LEMUR job needs a private root, not just a private DB.
nodes.norm_label: pod-local lemur root (shared scratch dir fix)

nodes.label: Single-writer SQLite-on-NFS rule
nodes.rationale: N writers on the NFSv3-hosted SQLite file corrupt it rather than blocking, so screen_and_train.py refuses --num-shards>1 without --screen-only, DB-writing stages stay single-pod, and jobs that write the real DB are queued rather than overlapped.

nodes.label: Strided (i % num_shards) candidate sharding
nodes.rationale: Ids are emitted in strategy round-robin order, so contiguous blocks would hand each shard a skewed strategy mix and make per-shard pass rates incomparable.

nodes.label: The screen gate is a label, not a filter
nodes.rationale: results_shard*.json records ep1 for every candidate that trains at all. The default 32.7 floor was measured on 18 hand-written models and LLM output has a far wider spread, so recording the full ep1 distribution lets the production gate be chosen from data and re-applied for free.
nodes.norm_label: the screen gate is a label, not a filter

nodes.label: preflight.py — CPU build+forward pre-screen
nodes.rationale: The 70% build/forward failure rate is a scheduling problem, not a prompt problem: each dead candidate consumed a GPU slot, dataset load and epoch start (~80 s) to report a shape error. Preflight checks parse → static contract → build → train_setup → forward on CPU at ~50 candidates per 4 s, replacing ~11.5 GPU-hours. It deliberately judges nothing else — a pass means 'not obviously dead', never 'will train'.

nodes.label: Not restarting the running screen to use preflight
nodes.rationale: Killing a screen ~1/3 done would discard ~6 GPU-hours to save about the same, and would lose the one chance to validate preflight against ground truth — the screen's own pass/fail set on the same 516 candidates.
nodes.norm_label: not restarting the running screen to use preflight

nodes.label: Static audits of generated code need AST, not regex
nodes.rationale: Two audit checks produced confidently false headlines: '503 candidates hardcode 256' came from a [^)]* regex stopping inside (1,3,256,256) — the real figure is 58 — and '7 call .to(device) without self.device' matched models correctly binding a local device. Same failure mode as the isinstance grep: matching the mention of a thing rather than its use.
nodes.norm_label: static audits of generated code need ast, not regex

nodes.label: norm_census.py — count constructed norms via ast.Call
nodes.rationale: The 'GA output is 100% BatchNorm' error came from a grep matching nn.BatchNorm2d inside an isinstance() NaN-guard tuple present in nearly every denoise template. Counting only ast.Call nodes makes that error unrepresentable rather than merely guarded against; validated against d10v2's known answer (92 norm-free / 1 BatchNorm of 93) before use.
nodes.norm_label: norm_census.py — count constructed norms via ast.call

nodes.label: analyse_screen.py — pool and analyse screen results
nodes.rationale: Reports each arm twice, with and without the 125 device-repaired candidates, so the arm comparison can be quoted without the prompt bug in it. Originally globbed only results_shard*.json, which would have broken the unsharded evolve loop.
nodes.norm_label: analyse_screen.py — pool and analyse screen results

nodes.label: GA run NORM-v3 (denoise-ga-normv3)
nodes.rationale: Asks whether norm-diverse seeds plus a mobile-safe norm mutation target move the normalisation axis at all, against d10v2's 88 norm-free / 1 BatchNorm baseline. Exactly two changes from d10v2 so the result is attributable, with fresh seed_ga_NORMv3_* paths because reusing d10v2's would resume that population at gen 8 with the old seeds.

nodes.label: layer_type norm-swap operator
nodes.rationale: It can only swap a norm that is already present, and 9 of 10 d10v2 seeds had no norm module at all — a no-op operator looks identical to a missing one in the output. Weight raised 0.15 → 0.25 in NORM-v3.

nodes.label: BRUTE_NORM_SAFE=1 mobile-safe norm targets
nodes.rationale: Restricts norm targets to {BatchNorm2d, Identity} and lists Identity as both source and target so the axis moves in both directions; previously it was a one-way ratchet toward norm-free.

nodes.label: Deliberately not using --edge-strict in NORM-v3
nodes.rationale: It would reject most descendants of the LayerNorm/GroupNorm/InstanceNorm seeds, which is the very thing being measured; observe first, label deployability after.

nodes.label: Norm-clone seed cluster (one backbone, norm swapped)
nodes.rationale: DenoiseGroupNorm/ResBN/LayerNorm/InstNorm all measure 3756.0 MMac / 0.73 Mp — the cos 0.94–0.998 cluster seeds_distinct.sh collapsed for diversity. For a norm experiment that redundancy is a controlled 4-way contrast where norm is the only variable, so reintroducing them was accidentally the right call.
nodes.norm_label: norm-clone seed cluster (one backbone, norm swapped)

nodes.label: DenoiseUNet2 edge-legality retraction
nodes.rationale: Written up in seeds_distinct.sh BEST10_V3 as the best model measured (35.368 last10) and edge-legal, it is 54618 MMac — ~6x the budget. The check that cleared it read source (transpose padding, norm modules) and a source-level read cannot see MACs, so its dB must not be quoted as a target for edge models.

nodes.label: LLM run denoise-llmgen-1 (2026-07-30)
nodes.rationale: 24-reference corpus (7 seeds + 17 families); parse rate 9/10 but end-to-end yield 1/10, the gap being that 'parsed' only means a class Net was recoverable from the text.

nodes.label: LLM run denoise-llmgen2 (516 parseable of 550)
nodes.rationale: 94% parseable is an upper bound, not a training rate: the 4-candidate smoke test had 2 raise at build/first-forward, and the completed screen showed only 28% actually run.

nodes.label: denoise-llmscreen2 result — arms fail alike, succeed differently
nodes.rationale: Both arms run ~28% of the time, so references do not help the model produce valid code; but of what runs, cold median is 13.05 dB (near-noise) against 31.23 dB seeded — references determine whether the architecture is any good, not whether it compiles. Excluding the 122 device-repaired cold candidates, the cold arm contributes nothing at all.
nodes.norm_label: denoise-llmscreen2 result — arms fail alike, succeed differently

nodes.label: Stage-2 epoch budget corrected 50 → 5
nodes.rationale: stat.epoch in the DB is epoch_max, a config key, not a per-epoch curve index: GA models have exactly one row at epoch_max=5 with the curve on disk under _epoch_stats/. Five epochs is nine times cheaper (~6 h vs ~52 h for 90 survivors) and directly comparable to the 223 GA models already in the DB, which is the whole point of running both generators. A separate top-K 50-epoch stage is named explicitly for headline dB claims.

nodes.label: Arm baked into the DB model name
nodes.rationale: Both arms previously wrote the same LLM_Denoise-* stem, making 'was this cold or seeded?' unanswerable once run dirs age out, since the DB name is the only thing that survives. Names are now LLM_Denoise_cold-<hash> / LLM_Denoise_seeded-<hash>.
nodes.norm_label: arm baked into the db model name

nodes.label: The DB records the final epoch, not the peak
nodes.rationale: The first stage-2 result peaked at epoch 4 (34.145) and settled to 33.527, so MAX(accuracy) over a model's rows is not 'peak during training'.
nodes.norm_label: the db records the final epoch, not the peak

nodes.label: curve_from JSON-shape bug (silent nan last5)
nodes.rationale: check_nn writes each per-epoch file as a list wrapping one dict; curve_from called d.get('accuracy') on the list, raising AttributeError into a bare `except Exception: pass`, so every curve came back empty and every last5 was nan while the DB rows were fine. It looked exactly like 'no per-epoch stats were produced'. Fixed by unwrapping the list, and the bare except now prints what it skipped.

nodes.label: Degenerate positive anchor in diversity calibration
nodes.rationale: All 24 WL-collision positives sit at cosine exactly 1.0 because the embedding is a function of the graph, so the anchor proves only 'identical implies 1.0' and says nothing about where near-duplicates sit. The negative anchor (distinct hand-written families, max 0.9213) matches diversity_gate.py's recorded 0.921 and does transfer to LLM output; only the positive side (>=0.985, from same-family mutants) is generator-specific. 0.93 is the lowest zero-false-merge floor and 0.95 the operating point, but the region 0.921–0.985 has no ground truth.
nodes.norm_label: degenerate positive anchor in diversity calibration

nodes.label: Quote single-linkage cluster count, not greedy accepts
nodes.rationale: DiversityGate is greedy so its answer depends on arrival order (105–113 over 20 shuffles at 0.95); clusters are order-independent. Headline: 91 distinct architectures of 186 traceable, single-linkage at 0.95.
nodes.norm_label: quote single-linkage cluster count, not greedy accepts

nodes.label: Missing behavioural (CKA) diversity anchor
nodes.rationale: Structural embedding cannot see 'different graph, same function'; residual CKA on trained models would supply the near-duplicate ground truth, and must wait for trained survivors because untrained CKA is dominated by init noise.

nodes.label: dataset_manifest.py — provenance labelling and git delta
nodes.rationale: Read-only by design: it labels every denoise model in the DB by provenance and reports what git has not seen, but never runs git add/commit/push — it writes a path list for the user to review. The cold/seeded split is unreconstructible from the DB name for older rows, so the manifest joins the arm in from generation candidate ids via the eval results.
nodes.norm_label: dataset_manifest.py — provenance labelling and git delta

nodes.label: git add -A deletion hazard (252,227 deleted files)
nodes.rationale: The worktree holds 116 directories where HEAD has 252k tracked files under ab/nn/stat/train/, so a blanket add would record a quarter-million deletions as a commit. push_list.txt therefore contains adds only, every path verified to exist on disk; deletions are counted and reported but never listed.
nodes.norm_label: git add -a deletion hazard (252,227 deleted files)

nodes.label: GA vs LLM throughput (models into DB per GPU-hour)
nodes.rationale: GA ~30.7 models/GPU-h against the LLM's 1.55 — ~20x — because the LLM's cost is dominated by the 94% of samples that never reach the DB. Two caveats: it measures entries per GPU-hour, not value per entry (the LLM reaches architectures no mutation operator can), and the 26 came from the pre-fix prompt, with preflight removing the 70% build failures from the GPU budget.
nodes.norm_label: ga vs llm throughput (models into db per gpu-hour)

nodes.label: The LLM has no generations, by construction
nodes.rationale: The GA is iterative with selection so quality compounds; the LLM run is one-shot i.i.d. sampling where prompt 550 knows nothing about prompt 1. Even the seeded arm references hand-written seeds, never the LLM's own output, so it is not a feedback loop.
nodes.norm_label: the llm has no generations, by construction

nodes.label: LLM EVOLVE — generation N+1 conditioned on N's survivors
nodes.rationale: Closes the structural gap with the GA by adding selection pressure to LLM sampling. Sequential and single-GPU by necessity: the training stages write the NFS-hosted SQLite DB, and generation N+1 depends on N's trained results so stages could not overlap anyway.
nodes.norm_label: llm evolve — generation n+1 conditioned on n's survivors

nodes.label: elite_archive.py — diversity-gated elite pool with seed floor
nodes.rationale: Ranks by last-3-epoch mean (not peak) and admits greedily under the WL/cosine gate: a pool picked purely on score collapses, since the top-K of a converging population are near-copies and conditioning on K copies is the LLM analogue of a GA losing diversity. Hand-written seeds stay eligible as a floor so the population cannot walk downhill, and it warns explicitly if a pool becomes all-hand-written, at which point the next generation is conditioning rather than evolving.
nodes.norm_label: elite_archive.py — diversity-gated elite pool with seed floor

nodes.label: PRIVATE_DB smoke testing
nodes.rationale: A smoke test sharing the DB is not a safe smoke test, so it runs against a pod-local DB copy; the GENS=1 N=4 run caught the results.json glob bug and a wrong-CWD bug before production.

nodes.label: Two roots: generation CWD vs train/screen CWD
nodes.rationale: ab/gpt/util/Const.py resolves conf/llm/*.json relative to CWD, so generation needs cwd=nn-gpt while train/screen needs the LEMUR root; each step now sets its own rather than inheriting one.
nodes.norm_label: two roots: generation cwd vs train/screen cwd

nodes.label: One-shot LLM approach stopped (all models 1.3–2.2 dB below hand-written)
nodes.rationale: Stopped after 8 of 26 complete models: best LLM 33.903 dB against DenoiseSubPixel's 35.246. The stop also prevented an over-cap 10787 MMac model already in the gen-1 elite pool from propagating as a reference into every subsequent generation.
nodes.norm_label: one-shot llm approach stopped (all models 1.3–2.2 db below hand-written)

nodes.label: The LLM path never checked the MAC budget
nodes.rationale: The GA enforces 9053 MMac twice (--seed-mac-cap on seeds, --edge-filter on children) while the LLM path enforced it nowhere: screen_and_train.py has no MAC check and elite_archive.py printed 'MAC CAP NOT ENFORCED: cost backend unimportable' because nn-dataset's ab package shadows nn-gpt's under the pod-local root. Same failure mode as the DenoiseUNet2 retraction — a prompt states the budget, but a prompt is a request, not a constraint.
nodes.norm_label: the llm path never checked the mac budget

nodes.label: MAC checks use edge_cost._mac_hooks, not thop/fvcore
nodes.rationale: Neither profiler is installed (the first audit reported all 9 UNMEASURABLE), and a different counter would give numbers not comparable to the GA's, which is the entire point of measuring against the same cap. Unmeasurable is treated as ineligible, never as legal — failing open is exactly how over-cap models got in.
nodes.norm_label: mac checks use edge_cost._mac_hooks, not thop/fvcore

nodes.label: Two over-cap LLM models left in the DB
nodes.rationale: They are not edge-legal and must not be counted in any edge claim, but were not removed because deleting DB rows is destructive and is the user's call; sweep_out/manifest/llm_macs.json lists them by id.
nodes.norm_label: two over-cap llm models left in the db

nodes.label: The 9053 MMac cap does not survive a literature check
nodes.rationale: The cap is circular — it says 'our models fit our cap' because it was drawn around our largest seed, with no hardware measurement. Normalised as kMAC/px it is 5.8x the heaviest published mobile denoiser, 20x the model running at 34 ms on a 2026 flagship NPU, and 54x MFDNet-S. Only 3 of the project's models land inside the published mobile envelope. Not re-capped unilaterally because that invalidates the seed pool, both GA arms and the LLM elite pool, but the figure should not be called an edge budget in the thesis without this caveat.
nodes.norm_label: the 9053 mmac cap does not survive a literature check

nodes.label: kMAC/pixel normalisation
nodes.rationale: Published mobile denoisers report at 720p or Full HD while this work reports at 256x256; the networks are fully convolutional so MACs scale linearly with pixel count, making MAC/pixel the only valid comparison.

nodes.label: Recommended measured MAC caps (aggressive / NPU-realistic / permissive)
nodes.rationale: Anchored to published models rather than to owned ones: 170–270 MMac@256 (MFDNet-S/NAFNet), ~450 (MAI'26 NPU student at 34 ms on Dimensity 9500), ~1550 (MFDNet-L, heaviest published).
nodes.norm_label: recommended measured mac caps (aggressive / npu-realistic / permissive)

nodes.label: DenoiseThunder — most defensible edge model owned
nodes.rationale: Literature-derived, 1274 MMac / 19.4 kMAC/px — inside the MFDNet-L tier — despite being ranked 10th of 10 on PSNR.
nodes.norm_label: denoisethunder — most defensible edge model owned

nodes.label: DenoiseSubPixel — best hand-written family (35.25 dB)
nodes.rationale: At 4247 MMac / 64.8 kMAC/px it is 2.7x outside the published mobile envelope, so the best-scoring seed is not edge-legal by literature standards.

nodes.label: chain B/D status log — arm B auto-resume
nodes.rationale: Records the chain supervisor detecting arm B as 'not done + not running' and resuming launch_B0.sh — the same not-done-and-not-running restart discipline as the production supervisor.
nodes.norm_label: chain b/d status log — arm b auto-resume
